purpose: Development-only reformulation of optional seeded diversity as an incumbent-preserving interruptible challenger. The completed two-arm endpoint remains available at all times; seeded search is never allowed to worsen final quality. Measure where challenger benefits become certifiable and the quality/compute Pareto frontier of bounded challenger evaluation before any new confirmation split is selected.
scope: Synthetic positive-monotone graph 2-CNF ROBDD ordering only. Development evidence only; no C589/C590/C591 holdout case may be used for fitting or threshold selection.

search_contract.seeded_start: 16 random permutations from RNG graph_seed+100000; eligible width <= min(natural_width,rcm_width)+2; among eligible maximize minimum normalized Kendall distance to natural and RCM, ties lower width then lexicographic; if none eligible choose minimum width then lexicographic
search_contract.neighborhood: all distinct one-variable remove-and-reinsert orders in deterministic existing i-then-j enumeration
search_contract.accept: after a complete local stage, accept the globally best candidate only if live nonterminal ROBDD nodes strictly improve; ties by allocated nodes then lexicographic order
search_contract.oracle: cross-order exact Hamming-rank equality plus direct exhaustive truth comparison in each endpoint's own relabeled coordinates

controller_architecture.incumbent: first complete the existing two-arm natural+RCM policy and retain its final endpoint permanently
controller_architecture.challenger: evaluate the seeded arm independently; every challenger candidate compilation is charged
controller_architecture.quality_rule: final output is always the best already verified endpoint among the two-arm incumbent and evaluated seeded orders; therefore optional challenger evaluation cannot cause positive quality regret versus two-arm
controller_architecture.positive_certificate: as soon as any evaluated seeded order has live_nodes < incumbent_two_live, a verified quality improvement exists and the controller may stop immediately with that order without finishing the local stage
controller_architecture.negative_stop: no finite unevaluated prefix is treated as a proof of no future benefit; any early negative stop is a value-of-computation decision and must report missed-benefit regret versus exhaustive challenger

offline_development_collection.reason: collect complete trajectories for development analysis only; deployment policies may stop earlier

prefix_policy_semantics: Starting after the seeded initial-order compile, evaluate at most B additional challenger candidate compilations. If a positive certificate occurs by B, return the best verified challenger endpoint observed; otherwise return the two-arm incumbent. B=0 still charges the seeded initial-order compile if the challenger is opened; a separate pure two-arm baseline opens no challenger and pays zero challenger compiles.
primary_reports: Prevalence and magnitude of exhaustive seeded challenger benefit over two-arm.
Distribution of first positive-certificate compile index among beneficial cases, including stage and candidate position.
For every fixed prefix B, total extra challenger compiles, recovered quality gain, missed-benefit regret versus exhaustive challenger, and zero-harm verification versus two-arm.
Pareto frontier of extra candidate compilations versus missed-benefit live-node regret, with pure two-arm and exhaustive challenger included.
No classifier, threshold, or adaptive policy is confirmation evidence on this development set. Any learned/sequential policy derived here requires a new untouched preregistered split.
